html:
The founding law of Sparta, a short text said to come from the Oracle of Delphi and credited to the lawgiver Lycurgus. It survives only as quoted by Plutarch, centuries later. Its date is uncertain; many put it in the 7th century BCE.

The text sets out:

  • cults of Zeus and Athena
  • a division of the people into tribes and smaller units
  • a council of thirty elders, the gerousia, including the two kings
  • regular meetings of an assembly of citizens, which had the final say

A later rider, said to have been added by two kings, let the elders and kings set aside a "crooked" decision of the assembly. The ephors, five officials elected each year, are not in the text and seem to have grown in power later.

The Great Rhetra is one of the oldest constitutions in Europe that gives a formal role to a citizen assembly. With the common messes and the rule over the helots, it shaped the Spartan state.
